scaling.note: READ OFF THE CANDIDATE: the Company's door is 220 px tall (y 350-570) and a doorway is about 2.0 m, so a 1.75 m man at the boardwalk line (y 600) is ~195-200 px; the near edge follows Room 1's slope (0.3 per row) to 275 at the frame's foot. Errata 54's shared zones (222/240/263) land in this range, which is what "architectural scale corrected" means: Thad belongs in the street without shrinking or swelling.

weathered.note: PHASE 1.5G: REBUILT LETTER BY LETTER (doc 36 Q123). 1.5F rotated the whole crop level and the letters still stepped up and down the way the old angled board left them, which is what reads as crooked. Each authored glyph is now MOVED by whole pixels against its line's measured slant -- never rotated, never resampled -- so both lines sit on one row: baseline spread 6 px -> 2 on CONSOLATION, 7 px -> 1 on IMPROVEMENT COMPANY. This is the base state: the same seeded dulling and flaking as Phase 1.5.

gilt.note: Act III. Doc 05 Part Two-B: 'Fresh gilt on the lettering.' PHASE 1.5G: cut from the SAME rebuilt lettering as the weathered state, so the two cannot differ in position or angle by a pixel. Set by doc 48's S2.

ordinary.note: PHASE 1.5E: THE BOARD IS PLATE. The freestanding notice board -- rough timber, two posts on the boardwalk, a plank cap, the ordinary pinned papers -- was painted into the environment by the Region A structural repair (art/staging/room-02/repair-a/repair-op.json, street-candidate-03). The ORDINARY state draws nothing over it; the plate IS the ordinary board.

funeral.note: Act III: ONLY the changed paper -- the Phase 1.5B aged funeral sheet, pinned centre-top on the SAME physical board (a sheet-only overlay, no board pixels). No copy invented; the notice's words are the LOOK line's. Set by doc 48's S2.

entrances.note: the east edge, by the road in, facing down the street

say: Half of it is two stories tall in front and one story deep.
The other half is real, and is doing better.
onEnterSay.note: His first sight of the town, and the words come from doc 05's THE FALSE FRONTS rather than being written fresh -- he has the opinion already; this is him having it out loud at the moment he first has it. AMENDED AFTER TYLER CHECKED IT AGAINST THE PLATE: the original said EVERY building was a false front, which the picture contradicts -- the saloon is a flat parapet with a low roof behind it, and the hotel beside it is genuinely two storeys with lit windows and real depth. The plate is signed off, so the writing yields, and the observation is better for it: the half that is real is the half with money, which is the town's whole economy in one line. Gated on T_SEEN_MAIN_STREET, which onEnter sets, so it plays once.

obstacles.note: THE NEAR HITCHING RAIL at the west end: a foreground object he cannot walk through. It is the occluder this street never had; until its mask is cut from an ACCEPTED plate he walks round it, not behind it.

PHASE 1.5G: THE TROUGH'S OWN LINE ON THE GROUND. Its base runs from (1983,798) at the west end to (2218,750) at the east -- measured at 8x -- so the strip y 748-806 is where the trough stands, and nobody may stand in it. Ground BEHIND it (mud_mid down to 748) and IN FRONT of it (mud_near from 806) both stay walkable, which is what `keepsGroundAbove` is for. The old rect started at the band boundary y 776 and left a wedge, up to 28 px deep at the east end, where a man stood in FRONT of the trough's base and the band still called him behind it -- and the trough clipped his shins there.

PHASE 1.5F/G: the east rail's ground line. Its posts' feet are at y 786 (near, x 2290-2312) and 812 (far, x 2550-2578), so the strip y 776-816 is the fence's own footing: nobody stands inside it, and the ground in front of it (from y 816) stays walkable. The band boundary at 776 is above both feet, so mud_mid is behind the rail and mud_near is in front of it with nothing ambiguous between.

PHASE 1.5G: THE BAR'S OWN LINE, and the answer to Tyler's first finding. The bar is drawn across y 640-682, and the far mud is walkable at those depths, so a click on the rail put Thad's FEET exactly where the bar is drawn -- a man standing on a fence. This strip is now his; the far mud above it (600-636, behind the fence) and the mid mud below it (690-776, behind the fence and clear of the bar) both stay walkable, so 'behind the rail' is still a place he can go.

onEnterWalkNote: OUT INTO THE ROAD, NOT ALONG THE BUILDINGS. He was walking to x3400 y640, which is the boardwalk edge in front of the claims-road exit and beside the map seller’s office -- he arrived and then sidled up against a wall. x3300 y706 is the middle of the street with the town in front of him, which is where a man stands when he has just walked into a town he has never seen. Clear of the assay office door at x3082-3144, clear of the map seller at x3140, and low enough to be in the road rather than on the walk.

occlusion.note: PHASE 1.5E: cut. The plane-1 mask is the authored silhouette of the trough and the east rail on street-candidate-03; the west rail (x 0-560) stays an obstacle only, its base below the frame; the porch posts remain uncut (nobody walks behind them: the boardwalk band is plane 0 and in front of nothing).

planes.note: PHASE 1.5G: CUT FROM THE ART, not drawn round it (tools/retrofit/phase15g-masks.py, plane-1-cut.json). The trough is segmented from the plate's own pixels and trimmed at its base line, so the mask hugs the object and the contact shadow -- which is ground, not an occluder -- is not in it; the rail is its three members as quads, because that is exactly what the rail is. One file, one source of occlusion for both.

proofPoints.note: behind the trough, above its base line: its far rim and body mask his feet
behind the rail, mid-span between the posts: the bar crosses him
where the pie woman stands, on the ground behind the rail: the bar crosses her lower legs -- the generic actor case, and nothing about it is Thad's

occlusion.clipPlaneNote: PHASE 1.5G: depth is read from the FOOT BASELINE and the mask is local to the objects. Each object's obstacle sits on ITS OWN base line, so the band boundary at y 776 no longer has to double as the depth boundary: above an object's line the ground is behind it (mud_far and mud_mid, plane 1, masked by the object's own silhouette where the two overlap), below it the ground is in front (mud_near, plane 0). A man left or right of the trough at the same depth is untouched, because the mask has no pixels there.
